title: Photosynthesis — Overview
text: Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants, algae, and some bacteria convert light energy into chemical energy stored in carbohydrates. In plants it occurs mainly in the chloroplasts of leaf cells and uses the pigment chlorophyll to absorb light, most strongly in the blue and red parts of the spectrum. The light-dependent reactions in the thylakoid membranes split water, release oxygen as a by-product, and produce ATP and NADPH. The light-independent reactions (the Calvin cycle) in the stroma use that ATP and NADPH to fix carbon dioxide into glucose. The simplified overall equation is: six carbon dioxide plus six water, using light energy, yields one glucose plus six oxygen.
